items.vn: (noun). A person who operates equipment or a machine.
items.example: ex: She's a radio operator

items.vn: (verb). to start an activity, especially an organized one
items.example: ex: The enemy launched an attack at sunrise.

items.vn: (noun). the quality of being open and without secrets.
items.example: ex: He says that there needs to be more transparency in the way the government operates.

items.vn: (adjective).  impossible to think of or to believe exists
items.example: ex: Those are the lives of almost unimaginable deprivation

items.vn: (adjective). Consisting of many different and connected parts
items.example: ex: The company has a complex organizational structure.

items.vn: (adjective). elaborate in structure or decoration.
items.example: ex:  You own a fancy place and drive a practically new jeep

items.vn: (verb). Ask authoritatively or brusquely.
items.example: ex: If you don't stand up and demand a change, he'll keep on doing it.

items.vn: (adverb). in a sincere or genuine way.
items.example: ex: I sincerely hope that we shall have a change of government

items.vn: (noun). a set of related measures or activities with a particular long-term aim.
items.example: ex: It's the most popular radio programme

items.vn: (noun). replacement
items.example: ex: Vitamins should not be used as a substitute for a healthy diet.

items.vn: (verb). Exceed; be greater than.
items.example: ex: Attendance is expected to surpass last year's record.

items.vn: (noun). The action of using something or the fact of being used.
items.example: ex: The tractor had been damaged by rough usage.

items.vn: (noun). a sum of money added to a person's wages as a reward for good performance.
items.example: ex: The product has the added bonus of providing extra vitamins.

items.vn: (verb). Make partial or minor changes to (something)
items.example: ex: We can help you modify an existing home or build a new one.

items.vn: (verb). fixed firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass; implanted
items.example: ex: The thorn was embedded in her thumb

items.vn: (noun). A raised level surface on which people or things can stand.
items.example: ex: He stepped up onto the platform and looked out into the audience.

items.vn: (noun). the basic physical and organizational structures
items.example: ex: She slumped on the infrastructure terminal, awaiting the results of the status checks.

items.vn: (adjective). fitting in well with a person's needs, activities, and plans.
items.example: ex: I phoned your office to confirm that this date is convenient

items.vn: (noun). A formal request to be considered for a position or to be allowed to do or have something
items.example: ex: All the same, she finally sent her application for the job

items.vn: (verb). Build or make (something, typically a building)
items.example: ex: They plan to construct a barn behind the house

items.vn: (noun). the practice or science of collecting and analysing numerical data in large quantities
items.example: ex: The most recent statistics show the disease to be diminishing.

items.vn: (noun). the money that you spend on something
items.example: ex: I'm still waiting for his last expense account.

items.vn: (verb). cause emotion to arise or come about.
items.example: ex: This business should generate a lot of revenue

items.vn: (adjective). extremely beautiful or carefully made
items.example: ex: His lips traced the line from her neck to her jaw with small, hot kisses, sending exquisite shivers through her

items.vn: (adjective). characterized by a fundamental weakness
items.example: ex: I'm flawed, but I will do my best

items.vn: (noun). the programs and other operating information used by a computer.
items.example: ex: the software industry is blooming

items.vn: (adjective). so different in nature as to be incapable of coexisting.
items.example: ex: This statement is totally incompatible with Sir Henry Daly's and is only one of many contradictions in the case

items.vn: (adjective). costing a lot; expensive.
items.example: ex: Major problems require costly repairs

items.vn: (noun). the action or process of making a way through or into something
items.example: ex: the plant grows in clear, still waters where there is strong sunlight penetration

items.vn: (noun). a person who buys goods from producers and sells them to retailers or consumers.
items.example: ex: we aim to maintain value for money by cutting out the middleman and selling direct

items.vn: (adjective). having or showing an intense and selfish desire for something, especially wealth or power.
items.example: ex: "You were very greedy," said the girl.

items.vn: (noun). A great victory or achievement.
items.example: ex: Her performance in the debate competition was an unmitigated triumph.

sections.title: Passage 1: History of Refrigeration
sections.html:
Vehicle

(noun). a thing used for transporting people or goods, especially on land, such as a car, truck, or cart.

ex: the vehicle was sent skidding across the road

refrigerator

(noun). a piece of electrical equipment in which food is kept cold so that it stays fresh

ex: Store fruit juice in the refrigerator.

transport

(verb). to move something somewhere

ex: The pipeline was constructed to transport oil across Alaska to ports on the coast.

utilize

(verb). Make practical and effective use of.

ex: The vitamins come in a form that is easily utilized by the body.

distribute

(verb). Supply (goods) to retailers.

ex: the books will be distributed free to local schools.

butter

(noun). a pale yellow edible fatty substance made by churning cream

ex: We were served scones with butter and jam.

commercial

(adjective). Concerned with or engaged in commerce.

ex: The commercial future of the company looks very promising.

chemical

(noun). a compound or substance that has been purified or prepared, especially artificially

ex: controversy arose over treatment of apples with this chemical

refrigerant

(noun). A substance used for refrigeration.

ex: one of the refrigerant pipes had burst

harmful

(adjective). causing damage or injury to somebody/something, especially to a person’s health or to the environment

ex: This group of chemicals is known to be harmful to people with asthma.

atmosphere

(noun). the mixture of gases that surrounds the earth

ex: The atmosphere in the room was so stuffy I could hardly breathe.

detrimental

(adjective). harmful

ex: These chemicals have a detrimental effect/impact on the environment.

ozone layer

(noun). a layer in the earth's stratosphere at an altitude of about 6.2 miles (10 km) containing a high concentration of ozone

ex: The ozone layer surrounding the earth protects our skin from being hurt by the ultraviolet rays.

term

(noun). a word or phrase used as the name of something

ex: He served a short term for drunk driving.

farmer

(noun). a person who owns or manages a farm.

ex: He is a beef cattle farmer.

refrigerate

(verb). subject (food or drink) to cold in order to chill or preserve it, typically by placing it in a refrigerator.

ex: refrigerate the dough for one hour

temperature

(noun). the measurement in degrees of how hot or cold a thing or place is

ex: Preheat the oven to a temperature of 200 degrees Celsius.

patent

(verb). a government authority or license conferring a right or title for a set period, especially the sole right to exclude others from making, using, or selling an invention.

ex: he took out a patent for an improved steam hammer

tramcar

(noun). a trolley car.

ex: Tramcars run through the streets of the city.

railroad

(noun). a track with rails on which trains run

ex: We live close to the railroad line.

technical

(adjective). connected with the practical use of machinery, methods, etc. in science and industry

ex: Personally, I found some parts of the book a little too technical to follow.

method

(noun). A particular procedure for accomplishing or approaching something

ex: Travelling by train is still one of the safest methods of transport.

economical

(adjective). cost-effective

ex: What's the most economical way of heating this building?

speedy

(adjective). done or occurring quickly.

ex: That's a speedy recovery

uniform

(adjective). remaining the same in all cases and at all times; unchanging in form or character.

ex: The office walls and furniture are a uniform grey.

block

(noun). A large solid piece of hard material, especially rock, stone, or wood,

ex: The museum is just six blocks away.

storage

(noun). the action or method of storing something for future use.

ex: The room lacked storage space

manufacture

(verb). mass-produce

ex: The report notes a rapid decline in manufactured goods.

trucking

(noun). the activity of transporting goods somewhere in a truck

ex: The railroads can't really compete with trucking companies.

refrigeration

(noun). subjecting food or drink to cold in order to chill or preserve it.

ex: The food will spoil without refrigeration.

roof-mounted

(adjective). fitted at the roof of the house

ex: The Sodeca roof-mounted fans can be adapted to any type of roof.

liquefy

(verb). to become liquid; to make something liquid

ex: When heated they liquefy

fresh

(adjective). (food) recently produced or picked and not frozen

ex: Those are fresh fruits

consumer

(noun). A person who purchases goods and services for personal use.

ex: The new rates will affect all consumers, including businesses.

demand

(noun). an insistent and peremptory request, made as if by right

ex: There was little demand for tickets.

dietary

(adjective). connected with or contained in the food that you eat and drink regularly

ex: She gives dietary advice for healthy skin and hair

associated

(adjective). (of a person or thing) connected with something else.

ex: She was prepared to take on the job, with all its associated risks.

soaring

(adjective). increasing

ex: the soaring crime rate is frightening

reform

(noun). the action or process of reforming an institution or practice.

ex: We should promote the reform of the divorce laws

regional

(adjective). Relating to or characteristic of a region

ex: The three nations competed for regional hegemony.

transportation

(noun). a system for carrying people or goods from one place to another using vehicles, roads, etc.

ex: the safe transportation of used nuclear fuel

urbanisation

(noun). the process of making an area more urban.

ex: he saw nature being destroyed by urbanization

enlarge

(verb). Make or become larger

ex: They've enlarged the kitchen by building over part of the garden.

extensive

(adjective). Covering or affecting a large area.

ex: Her knowledge of music is extensive (= she knows a lot about music).

spread

(noun). the fact or process of spreading over an area.

ex: warmer temperatures could help reduce the spread of the disease

treatment

(noun). the manner in which someone behaves toward or deals with someone or something.

ex: the film's treatment of rural life is good

sewage

(noun). used water and waste substances that are produced by human bodies, that are carried away from houses and factories through special pipes

ex: the sewage treatment system is not good

dumping

(noun). the act or practice of dumping something, especially dangerous substances

ex: They have promised to limit the dumping of sewage sludge in the sea.

adverse

(adjective). preventing success or development;

ex: taxes are having an adverse effect on production

sector

(noun). An area or portion that is distinct from others.

ex: In the financial sector, banks and insurance companies have both lost a lot of money.

dairy

(noun). milk, eggs, cheese and other milk products

ex: It's a dairy farmer

mechanical

(adjective). Operated by a machine or machinery.

ex: The company produces mechanical parts for airplane engines.

substance

(noun). A particular kind of matter with uniform properties.

ex: What sort of substance could withstand those temperatures?

liquid

(noun). a substance that flows freely and is not a solid or a gas, for example water or oil

ex: Mercury is a liquid at room temperature.

cycle

(noun). A series of events that are regularly repeated

ex: A thousand people took part in the region's biggest-ever cycle race.

vapour

(noun). a mass of very small drops of liquid in the air

ex: The hollow glass tank contains hot mercury vapour.

compression

(noun). the action of compressing or being compressed.

ex: Compression fractures of the spine are common in older people.

absorption

(noun). the process or action by which one thing absorbs or is absorbed by another.

ex: her absorption in the problems of the Third World

steam

(noun). the vapor into which water is converted when heated, forming a white mist of minute water droplets in the air.

ex: That's a cloud of steam

jet

(noun). a jet engine.

ex: We flew to New York by jet.

ejector

(noun). a device that causes something to be removed or to drop out.

ex: It's a built-in drill ejector

cellar

(noun). an underground room often used for storing things

ex: he spent years building up a remarkable cellar of aged Riojas

spoilage

(noun). the decay of food which means that it can no longer be used

ex: The refrigerator air purifier reduces food spoilage and waste.

dissolve

(verb). to make a solid become part of a liquid

ex: Dissolve two spoons of powder in warm water.

saltpeter

(noun). a salty-tasting white powder used to preserve meat, and also used in producing explosives and fertilizers

ex: But pouring saltpeter from the minarets hasn't worked.

liquor

(noun). strong alcoholic drink

ex: Instinct told her his threat wasn't simply the liquor talking

fashionable

(adjective). representing a current popular style. (hợp thời trang)

ex: I don't think it would be fashionable if I wore a ski mask.

potential

(noun). having or showing the capacity to develop into something in the future.

ex: the crane operator's clear view reduces the potential for accidents

container

(noun). an object that can be used to hold or transport something.

ex: It's a microwaveable glass container

distribute

(verb). Supply (goods) to retailers.

ex: With information, we will distribute better.

initiate

(verb). Cause (a process or action) to begin.

ex: Leopold had wisely decided to initiate a conciliatory policy in Hungary.

evaporation

(noun). the process of a liquid changing or being changed into a gas

ex: There was evaporation of water from the leaf.

vacuum

(noun). a space that is completely empty of all substances, including all air or other gas

ex: the political vacuum left by the death of the Emperor

partial

(adjective). not complete or whole

ex: His latest play was deemed only a partial success by the critics

portable

(adjective). able to be easily carried or moved, especially because being of a lighter and smaller version than usual

ex: It's a portable television

compressor

(noun). a machine that compresses air or other gases

ex: The compressor may be driven by a steam engine or in any other convenient manner.

bunker

(noun). a strongly built shelter for soldiers or guns, usually underground

ex: That's a coal bunker

circulate

(verb). move or cause to move continuously or freely through a closed system or area

ex: Rumors are circulating around town

gravity

(noun). The force that attracts a body towards the centre of the earth,

ex: Gravity is what keeps everything from floating around.

flap

(noun). a piece of something thin, such as cloth, paper, or metal, hinged or attached only on one side, that covers an opening or hangs down from something.

ex: A small flap of skin can be seen above the wound.

cargo

(noun). goods carried on a ship, aircraft, or motor vehicle.

ex: The ship was carrying a cargo of wood.

synthetic

(adjective). (of a substance) made by chemical synthesis, especially to imitate a natural product

ex: That is synthetic rubber.

prevailing

(adjective). Existing at a particular time; current.

ex: The prevailing winds are from south to west.

devastation

(noun). great destruction or damage, especially over a wide area

ex: the floods caused widespread devastation

application

(noun). the action of putting something into operation.

ex: The design has many applications.

vicinity

(noun). the area near or surrounding a particular place.

ex: The number of people living in the immediate vicinity was small

sections.title: Passage 2: Ancient People in Sahara
sections.html:
engrave

(verb). cut or carve (a text or design) on the surface of a hard object

ex: That's a faintly southern accent

passage

(noun). a short extract from a book or other printed material

ex: he picked up the newspaper and read the passage again

fertile

(adjective). that plants grow well in

ex: There is an abundance of fertile soil and magnificent grazing land.

barren

(adjective). not good enough for plants to grow on it

ex: The site of the town is a barren, rocky mountain valley.

flank

(noun). the side of something such as a building or mountain

ex: Having reached the left flank, instead of going to the front where the firing was, he began to look for the general

southern

(adjective). situated in the south or directed toward or facing the south.

ex: The heavy Southern day reminded her of the Caribbean

remains

(noun). the parts left over after other parts have been removed, used, or destroyed

ex: the remains of a sandwich lunch were on the table

desert

(noun). a place with sand, hot weather and no vegetation

ex: The desert night was cold and dark.

slope

(noun). an area of land that is part of a mountain or hill

ex: hey waited until he climbed up the slope to where they stood

dune

(noun). asmall hill of sand formed by the wind, near the sea or in a desert

ex: They climbed the dune and kneeled close to the top

scatter

(verb). Throw in various random directions.

ex: Scatter the onions over the fish.

cooperate

(verb). work jointly toward the same end.

ex: the leaders promised to cooperate in ending the civil war

archaeological

(adjective). Relating to archaeology.

ex: An Austrian Archaeological Institute was founded in 1898

ancient

(adjective). Belonging to the very distant past and no longer in existence.

ex: It looked ancient, and he opened it carefully.

acquaint

(verb). to make somebody/yourself familiar with or aware of something

ex: This class is designed to acquaint students with the region's most important writers.

exploration

(noun). the act of travelling through a place in order to find out about it

ex: She was staring at him when his visual exploration was over.

initial

(adjective). Existing or occurring at the beginning.

ex: Her initial reaction was an urge to crawl under the table.

sketch

(verb). make a rough drawing of

ex: as they talked, Modigliani began to sketch her

destined

(adjective). regarded as developing as though according to a pre-existing plan.

ex: His sister, Katie, had insisted that they were destined to be together

site

(noun). A place where a particular event or activity is occurring or has occurred

ex: We're going to the site tonight.

nomad

(noun). a member of a community that moves with its animals from place to place

ex: The Yuruks on the contrary are a truly nomad race

roam

(verb). Move about or travel aimlessly

ex: He roamed about in search of work

excavate

(verb). ) Make (a hole or channel) by digging.

ex: They excavated an ancient city.

tomb

(noun). A large vault, typically an underground one, for burying the dead.

ex: His tomb is in the churchyard

skeleton

(noun). An internal or external framework of bone, cartilage, or other rigid material

ex: They found the fossil skeleton of a mastodon.

research

(noun). the systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources in order to establish facts and reach new conclusions

ex: she conducted research into the cause of Alzheimer's disease

laboratory

(noun). A room or building equipped for scientific experiments

ex: After introductions, Dean was led to a laboratory in the rear of the building

bundle

(verb). tie or roll up (a number of things) together as though into a parcel.

ex: she quickly bundled up her clothes

burial

(adjective). the act or ceremony of burying a dead body

ex: He deserves a burial of some sort.

estimate

(verb). to form an idea of the cost, size, value etc. of something, but without calculating it exactly

ex: We need to estimate how much paint we'll need for the job

compactly

(adverb). in a way that uses or fills only a small amount of space

ex: the work now went on expeditiously, unnecessary things were left, and the most valuable packed as compactly as possible.

artefact

(noun). an object that is made by a person, especially something of historical or cultural interest

ex: The limestone and marble foyer was lined with artifacts

approximately

(adverb). almost, but not completely

ex: It was a small white bone approximately one inch long.

industrious

(adjective). diligent and hard-working.

ex: an industrious people striving to make their country prosperous

forearm

(noun). the part of the arm between the elbow and the wrist

ex: She covered her eyes with one forearm and succumbed to tears.

strenuous

(adjective). requiring or using great effort or exertion.

ex: Fighting thereupon ceased. Her lean body handled the strenuous task easily

muscle

(noun). a piece of body tissue that you contract and relax in order to move a particular part of the body; the tissue that forms the muscles of the body

ex: he had muscle but no brains

attachment

(noun). a strong feeling of affection for somebody/something

ex: I feel no attachment to the countryside.

lifestyle

(noun). the way in which a person lives.

ex: Taking on an infant would mean a massive lifestyle change.

observation

(noun). the act of watching somebody/something carefully for a period of time

ex: she was brought into the hospital for observation

infer

(verb). to reach an opinion or decide that something is true on the basis of information that is available

ex: You can infer the meaning of the word from the context of the rest of the sentence.

presume

(verb). suppose that something is the case on the basis of probability.

ex: I presumed that the man had been escorted from the building

herder

(noun). a person who looks after a herd of livestock or makes a living from keeping livestock, especially in open country.

ex: they are nomadic cattle herders by tradition

consistent

(adjective). acting or done in the same way over time, especially so as to be fair or accurate.

ex: Her speed was consistent, her destination clear.

scholar

(noun). A specialist in a particular branch of study,

ex: He became a good Hungarian scholar.

dominant

(adjective). Having power and influence over others.

ex: The fold in the ears was caused by a heritable, dominant, mutated gene.

goat

(noun). a hardy domesticated ruminant animal that has backward curving horns and (in the male) a beard

ex: His interest in the goat dairy had brought him to her in the beginning.

transitional

(adjective). relating to or characteristic of a process or period of transition.

ex: a transitional government was appointed

professor

(noun). a university teacher of the highest rank

ex: Fred took on the air of a learned professor as he explained.

palaeontologist

(noun). a person who studies fossils

ex: Sperry was an avid paleontologist and displayed his large fossil collection in his home

toffee

(noun). a kind of firm or hard candy that softens when sucked or chewed, made by boiling together sugar and butter, often with other ingredients or flavorings added

ex: The mixture will solidify into toffee.

massive

(adjective). Large and heavy or solid.

ex: Massive maple trees shaded back and front.

inexorable

(adjective). that cannot be stopped or changed

ex: Napoleon was inexorable in his demands, and Pius VII.

prestigious

(adjective). respected and admired as very important or of very high quality

ex: The dinner reception is going to have a prestigious speaker present during the meal.

obsessive

(adjective). Of the nature of an obsession.

ex: She was a very obsessive woman too, a far different person than we were all led to believe.

perspective

(noun). A particular attitude towards something; a point of view

ex: When he spoke, his perspective surprised her

willingly

(adverb). in a willing way

ex: She hadn't discussed anything with him willingly so far.

alligator

(noun). a large semiaquatic reptile similar to a crocodile but with a broader and shorter head

ex: So the alligator comes out of the mud with quakings of the earth

civilization

(noun). a state of human society that is very developed and organized

ex: He went to study the civilization of the Arab world.

hippo

(noun). another term for hippopotamus.

ex: Hippos must submerge regularly because their skin is thin and virtually hairless and therefore vulnerable to overheating and dehydration.

vicinity

(noun). the area near or surrounding a particular place.

ex: In the vicinity are several fine mansions.

exhume

(verb). to remove a dead body from the ground especially in order to examine how the person died

ex: Azemi obtained a court order to exhume the body and arrested the brother

femur

(noun). the bone of the thigh or upper hind limb, articulating at the hip and the knee.

ex: There is a slight ridge on the femur in the place of a third trochanter.

coincide

(verb). Occur at the same time.

ex: The belt of folding does not precisely coincide with this central sea, but the correspondence is fairly close

contrast

(noun). The state of being strikingly different from something else

ex: I observed an interesting contrast in the teaching styles of the two women.

ridge

(noun). a narrow area of high land along the top of a line of hills; a high pointed area near the top of a mountain

ex: They would have to walk along the ridge for a while to get there

laborious

(adjective). taking a lot of time and effort

ex: Away from his father he maintained his laborious habits.

cemetery

(noun). A large burial ground, especially one not in a churchyard.

ex: If he were in a grave—in a cemetery somewhere—I could go there and put flowers on it.

cattle

(noun). domesticated animals , which give meat and milk

ex: I could run a passel of cattle on that land.

pastoralist

(noun). a sheep or cattle farmer.

ex: Milk products typical of nomadic pastoralists formed the mainstay of their diet

slaughter

(noun). the killing of animals for

ex: thousands of calves were exported to the continent for slaughter

sections.title: Passage 3: Texting the Television
sections.html:
Factor

(noun). a circumstance or a fact

ex: The other factor was that he was doing what he had always dreamed of doing

relevant

(adjective). Closely connected or appropriate to what is being done

ex: Some children like to think that the rules are not relevant to them.

interactive

(adjective). (of two people or things) influencing each other.

ex: The cost of interactive information exchange, such as asking questions about products you are contemplating purchasing, has fallen to nearly zer

phenomenon

(noun). A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen,

ex: There are UFO groups which investigate the UFO phenomenon

attribute

(verb). regard something as being caused by (someone or something).

ex: he attributed the firm's success to the efforts of the managing director

majority

(noun). The greater number.

ex: It's also covered by the majority of Memon's army.

broadcaster

(noun). an organization that transmits a programme or information by radio or television.

ex: Channel 4 is the only terrestrial broadcaster to have received no support - yet.

supernatural

(adjective). attributed to some force beyond scientific understanding

ex: Some humans are born with unique, supernatural talents

revenue

(noun). income, especially when of an organization (doanh thu, kết quả kinh doanh)

ex: The factory lost revenue because of the strike by the workers.

appreciable

(adjective). large or important enough to be noticed.

ex: Tea and coffee both contain appreciable amounts of caffeine

certain

(adjective). specific but not explicitly named or stated.

ex: He raised certain personal problems with me

profit

(noun). the money that you make in business or by selling things, especially after paying the costs involved

ex: The company made a profit this year.

rival

(adjective). competing with other people, companies, products, etc. for the same thing or in the same area

ex: Any rival bidder will have to move quickly and pay considerably more.

induce

(verb). Succeed in persuading or leading (someone) to do something.

ex: The advertisement is meant to induce people to eat more fruit.

consultancy

(noun). a company that gives expert advice on a particular subject to other companies or organizations

ex: We are an engineering consultancy that requires a cost accountant.

participant

(noun). a person who is taking part in an activity or event

ex: You sure seemed like a willing participant for a while there.

cryptic

(adjective). having a meaning that is mysterious or obscure.

ex: he found his boss's utterances too cryptic

crossword

(noun). a puzzle consisting of a grid of squares and blanks into which words crossing vertically and horizontally are written according to clues.

ex: she settled down to do the crossword

considerable

(adjective). Notably large in size, amount, or extent.

ex: His note pad was ever present and he spent a considerable amount of time on the phone.

proportion

(noun). A part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole.

ex: His ears were drawn out of proportion with his head.

satisfactory

(adjective). fulfilling expectations or needs; acceptable, though not outstanding or perfect.

ex: The job requires a satisfactory level of performance

unexpectedly

(adverb). In a way that was not expected or regarded as likely.

ex: In September 1665 the king unexpectedly paid him a visit at Wimborne.

massive

(adjective). Large and heavy or solid.

ex: Massive maple trees shaded back and front.

indispensable

(adjective). absolutely necessary.

ex: he made himself indispensable to the parish priest

grumble

(verb). complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

ex: After that, my stomach was grumbling and everyone else was groaning about their hunger

database

(noun). a structured set of data held in a computer, especially one that is accessible in various ways.

ex: The database covers nine million workers

bypass

(verb). a road passing around a town or its center to provide an alternative route for through traffic.

ex: I had a bypass last year so have been building up my strength

code

(noun). A system of words, letters, figures, or symbols used to represent others,

ex: The Americans cracked their diplomatic code

crucial

(adjective). Decisive or critical, especially in the success or failure of something

ex: Vitamins are crucial for maintaining good health.

aspect

(noun). A particular feature of something

ex: The house had escaped the fire; it showed signs of damage but its general aspect was unchanged.

emergence

(noun). the fact of somebody/something coming out from a dark, confined or hidden place

ex: As a result of this emergence the stratigraphic break between the Ordovician and the Silurian is one of the greatest in the whole Palaeozoic group.

digit

(noun). Any of the numerals from 0 to 9, especially when forming part of a number.

ex: Pulling out the letter, she looked at the ten digit key code

compatible

(adjective). able to exist or be used together without causing problems

ex: I thought I was marrying a man who had chosen a lifestyle compatible with mine.

universal

(adjective). involving all the people in the world

ex: Death is the most universal experience possible, true, but it's also the most personal.

perspective

(noun). A particular attitude towards something; a point of view

ex: When he spoke, his perspective surprised her

enlarge

(verb). Make or become larger

ex: They've enlarged the kitchen by building over part of the garden.

dilemma

(noun). a situation which makes problems, often one in which you have to make a very difficult choice between things of equal importance

ex: He made an attempt to resolve the long-standing dilemma.

margin

(noun). an amount by which a thing is won or falls short.

ex: She escaped death by a narrow margin

medium

(noun). a way of communicating information, etc. to people

ex: They told the story through the medium of dance.

reluctance

(noun). the feeling of being unwilling to do something

ex: He tossed in a hint of reluctance, just for good measure.

content

(adjective). In a state of peaceful happiness.

ex: I'm content to just move forward.

alter

(verb). change in significant way

ex: He pronounced the words that would forever alter her life.

operator

(noun). A person who operates equipment or a machine.

ex: She's a radio operator

launch

(verb). to start an activity, especially an organized one

ex: The enemy launched an attack at sunrise.

transparency

(noun). the quality of being open and without secrets.

ex: He says that there needs to be more transparency in the way the government operates.

unimaginable

(adjective). impossible to think of or to believe exists

ex: Those are the lives of almost unimaginable deprivation

complex

(adjective). Consisting of many different and connected parts

ex: The company has a complex organizational structure.

fancy

(adjective). elaborate in structure or decoration.

ex: You own a fancy place and drive a practically new jeep

demand

(verb). Ask authoritatively or brusquely.

ex: If you don't stand up and demand a change, he'll keep on doing it.

sincerely

(adverb). in a sincere or genuine way.

ex: I sincerely hope that we shall have a change of government

programme

(noun). a set of related measures or activities with a particular long-term aim.

ex: It's the most popular radio programme

substitute

(noun). replacement

ex: Vitamins should not be used as a substitute for a healthy diet.

surpass

(verb). Exceed; be greater than.

ex: Attendance is expected to surpass last year's record.

usage

(noun). The action of using something or the fact of being used.

ex: The tractor had been damaged by rough usage.

bonus

(noun). a sum of money added to a person's wages as a reward for good performance.

ex: The product has the added bonus of providing extra vitamins.

modify

(verb). Make partial or minor changes to (something)

ex: We can help you modify an existing home or build a new one.

embed

(verb). fixed firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass; implanted

ex: The thorn was embedded in her thumb

platform

(noun). A raised level surface on which people or things can stand.

ex: He stepped up onto the platform and looked out into the audience.

infrastructure

(noun). the basic physical and organizational structures

ex: She slumped on the infrastructure terminal, awaiting the results of the status checks.

convenient

(adjective). fitting in well with a person's needs, activities, and plans.

ex: I phoned your office to confirm that this date is convenient

application

(noun). A formal request to be considered for a position or to be allowed to do or have something

ex: All the same, she finally sent her application for the job

construct

(verb). Build or make (something, typically a building)

ex: They plan to construct a barn behind the house

statistics

(noun). the practice or science of collecting and analysing numerical data in large quantities

ex: The most recent statistics show the disease to be diminishing.

expense

(noun). the money that you spend on something

ex: I'm still waiting for his last expense account.

generate

(verb). cause emotion to arise or come about.

ex: This business should generate a lot of revenue

exquisite

(adjective). extremely beautiful or carefully made

ex: His lips traced the line from her neck to her jaw with small, hot kisses, sending exquisite shivers through her

flawed

(adjective). characterized by a fundamental weakness

ex: I'm flawed, but I will do my best

software

(noun). the programs and other operating information used by a computer.

ex: the software industry is blooming

incompatible

(adjective). so different in nature as to be incapable of coexisting.

ex: This statement is totally incompatible with Sir Henry Daly's and is only one of many contradictions in the case

costly

(adjective). costing a lot; expensive.

ex: Major problems require costly repairs

penetration

(noun). the action or process of making a way through or into something

ex: the plant grows in clear, still waters where there is strong sunlight penetration

middlemen

(noun). a person who buys goods from producers and sells them to retailers or consumers.

ex: we aim to maintain value for money by cutting out the middleman and selling direct

greedy

(adjective). having or showing an intense and selfish desire for something, especially wealth or power.

ex: "You were very greedy," said the girl.

triumph

(noun). A great victory or achievement.

ex: Her performance in the debate competition was an unmitigated triumph.
